Ireland's economy grew 12.3% on this map. Germany's grew 0.2%. Same continent, same euro. Why do Ireland's numbers look so strange?

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The map shows real GDP growth per year. Ireland 12.3%, Poland and Turkey 3.6%, Spain 2.8%, France 0.8%, Germany 0.2%. Data: World Bank (2023-25).

2/ Ireland is famous for odd growth figures. In July 2016 its statistics office revised 2015 growth to 26.3%. Paul Krugman reacted within minutes and the episode became known as 'leprechaun economics'.
3/ The jump traced to a single transaction in early 2015, tied to Apple's restructuring, not to a sudden burst of factories or shops.
4/ Trade tells the same story. Exports plus imports equal 240% of Irish GDP, against 79% in Germany and 34% in Russia. Data: World Bank (2023-25).
5/ Ireland now publishes a modified measure, GNI*, built to strip out multinational distortions. For 2017, Irish GDP was about 162% of GNI*.
6/ So read 12.3% with care: huge growth in a small, multinational-heavy economy does not necessarily mean everyday incomes jumped.
Which of these surprised you most? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
